subject: history_social
passage: Kangchenjunga, on the border of Nepal and the Indian state of Sikkim, is the third-highest mountain in the world. When British climbers George Band and Joe Brown made the first ascent in 1955, they stopped a few steps below the top, keeping a promise made to the ruler of Sikkim that the summit, which local people regarded as sacred, would not be stepped on. Many ______ later expeditions have honored the same tradition, turning back just short of the highest point.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The later expeditions belong to many climbers, so a plural possessive is needed. A plural noun ending in s shows possession with an apostrophe after the s: "climbers' later expeditions."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Climber's" is singular, but "Many" shows that more than one climber is meant.
explanation.B: Correct. "Climbers'" is the plural possessive, matching "Many."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Climbers" has no apostrophe, so it cannot show that the expeditions belong to the climbers; "Many climbers later expeditions" does not make sense.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Climbers's" is not a standard form; a plural ending in s takes only an apostrophe.
